newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end mixed in thinly-traded session.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end mixed in thinly-traded session.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures ended narrowly mixed, with speculative buying giving the most-active November contract a slight nudge higher in late-session dealings, market sources said.
Activity remained dull as volume was estimated at only 1,000 lots.
November FCOJ settled up 0.20 cent at 106.00 cents a lb after trading from 106.80 to 105.25, also the low made Wednesday. The remaining months closed down 0.70 to up 1.55.
Support for November contract was maintained between the recent low of 103.00 hit Sept 5, and resistance was seen between 110.00 and 112.00.
Analysts said prices could head lower, citing weak technical indicators.
"The RSI (Relative Strength Index) is around 40 and dropping, the stochastics are still in a downtrend...everything seems to be low for juice," said Kevin Marshburn, an analyst with Fimat Futures.

He said frozen concentrated orange juice futures prices typically rally late in the summer, when inventories begin to drop. But he did not cite a fundamental culprit was for this season's low prices. "It's all spec selling. The trend is just different this year," he said.
Traders await the USDA's Florida crop estimate in about six weeks for fundamental direction. Expectations for the crop remain around 215 million 90-lb boxes.
